newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada has ads for replacement workers.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada has ads for replacement workers.

text.p: Air Canada confirmed on Thursday that it was seeking to hire replacement workers in the event that its 3,300 sales and tickets agents go on strike December 5.
Air Canada spokeswoman Kym Robertson told Reuters that the airline had placed advertisements in several Canadian newspapers seeking temporary employees.
"The issue here is that we have an obligation to our customers. We will operate a full schedule, business as ususal," Robertson said.

Earlier Thursday, the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union representing the Air Canada sales and ticket agents, accused the carrier of using "scab" workers to intimidate the union membership into accepting the company's contract demands.
The company and the union are scheduled to resume talks on December 2. The union membership voted 91 percent in favour of taking strike action if an agreement was not reached by December 5.
"Hopefully, we will get a deal before midnight on December 5," Robertson said.
The contract for the 3,300 Air Canada employees expired on September 30. Both sides agreed to allow a government conciliation process to run its course, Robertson said.
